statement.p: Suppose that z is a linear function of x and y with slope 5 in the x direction and slope 1 in the y direction.
(a) A change of -0.3 in x and -0.4 in y produces what change in z?
(b) If z=5 when x=3 and y=4, what is the value of z when x=2.7 and y=3.9?

static.solution:
(a) Since z is a linear function of x and y with slope 5 in the x direction, and slope 1 in the y direction, we have: z = 5 x + 1 y + c. We can write an equation for changes in z in terms of changes in x and y: \Delta z = (5 (x + \Delta x) + 1(y + \Delta y) + c) - (5 x + 1 y + c) = 5 \Delta x + 1 \Delta y. Since \Delta x = -0.3 and \Delta y = -0.4, we have \Delta z = 5 (-0.3) + 1(-0.4) = -1.9. So a -0.3 change in x and a -0.4 change in y produces a -1.9 change in z.
(b) As we know that z=5 when x=3 and y=4, the value of z when x=2.7 and y=3.9 will be z = 5 + \Delta z = 5 + 5\Delta x + 1\Delta y. where \Delta z is the change in z when x changes from 3 to 2.7 and y changes from 4 to 3.9. We have \Delta x = 2.7 - 3 = -0.3 and \Delta y = 3.9 - 4 = -0.1. Therefore, when x=2.7 and y=3.9, we have z = 5 + 5 \cdot(-0.3) + 1\cdot(-0.1) = 3.4.
